<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
Hello,
Found a potential data race in `client-go` testing.
There is a test `TestWatchCallNonNamespace`
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture_test.go#L56
If we update it like this (we actually can do it [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture.go#L97)):
```
...
go func() {
	err := o.Create(testResource, testObj, ns)
	if err != nil {
		t.Errorf("test resource creation failed: %v", err)
	}
	// Potential data race
	_, err = o.Get(testResource, ns, testObj.GetName())
	if err != nil {
		t.Errorf("test resource getting failed: %v", err)
	}
}()
out := <-watch.ResultChan()
// Modify received object
// Potential data race
outCasted := out.Object.(*unstructured.Unstructured)
outCasted.Object["data"] = strconv.Itoa(rand.Int())
...
```
If watcher updates received object we get a data race.

#### What you expected to happen:
No data race

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

#### Anything else we need to know?:
My suggestion: send copy of object here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture.go#L403
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture.go#L419
comments:
Hi @novahe,
Did you run my test with `-race` flag?

Of course if I comment 
`// obj = obj.DeepCopyObject()` 
there will be data race.

But let's take a look at:
1. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5fe522c2376e9a732a50c89f38986ce4300fd4a0/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture.go#L416-L420
We _store_ `obj` in `t.objects` and do `w.Add(..)` with the _same_ `obj`. So, watcher receives `obj` that is stored in `t.objects` map.

2. If we call `o.Get(...)` we take the same `obj` from `t.objects`:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5fe522c2376e9a732a50c89f38986ce4300fd4a0/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture.go#L287-L295
Therefore, if watcher modifies received `obj` in another goroutine we have data race. 

Output:
```
==================

Write at 0x00c0002ea660 by goroutine 8:
  runtime.mapassign_faststr()
      /usr/local/go/src/runtime/map_faststr.go:202 +0x0

  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime.DeepCopyJSON()

  k8s.io/client-go/testing.(*tracker).Get()
      /home/art/go/src/github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture.go:295 +0x2bb
  k8s.io/client-go/testing.TestWatchCallAndModifyNonNamespace.func1()
```

Hi @glazychev-art,
You're right ,thank you for solving my confusion.  
One solution could be to copy of `obj`, I will try to fix it.

if there are multiple watchers, and they modify the object in their delete handler, they should not observe each other's modifications
